
  canyon dev · claims-portal v1.3 → prod · localhost:7777

  Reviewing v1.3 again under today's rules. Preview is not touched.

  Review

  ✗ Review blocked · 1 blocking finding

  Nothing was built and nothing was deployed.

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  critical  Found a Stripe Access Token, posing a risk to payment processing services and sensitive financial data
  apps/web/src/lib/payments.ts:14:1

    14 │ ••••
       │ ^^^^

  Found a Stripe Access Token, posing a risk to payment processing services
  and sensitive financial data. stripe-access-token has detected secret for
  file apps/web/src/lib/payments.ts.

  fix   Rotate this credential — it has been in your code. If nothing reads
        it, delete it from the code; otherwise store the new one with canyon
        secret set STRIPE_ACCESS_TOKEN and read it from the environment.
  why   Policy "No secrets in the code"

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  high  /api/admin/policies is reachable without a session
  apps/web/src/app/api/admin/policies/route.ts:8:3

     8 │   return NextResponse.json(await db.policies.forOrg(params.orgId));
       │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

  There's no session check in the handler, and middleware.ts:22 leaves
  /api/admin/policies out of the matcher — so nothing upstream is checking
  either. Any caller without a session gets what this handler returns.

  fix   Either add /api/admin/policies to the middleware matcher, or return
        early from the handler when the request has no cp_session cookie. The
        matcher is the safer of the two — it covers routes nobody's written
        yet.
  why   Policy "Every route needs sign-in"

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  high  /api/session starts a session without checking one
  apps/web/src/app/api/session/route.ts:8:3

     8 │   res.cookies.set("cp_session", String(form.get("email") ?? "adjuster"), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/" });
       │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

  It sets the cp_session cookie, so whoever it lets through gets a session. A
  sign-in that verifies who is signing in first has to work this way; a dev
  login, an impersonation route, or a password check a flag switches off lets
  anyone in as anyone.

  fix   Set the cp_session cookie only after the handler has verified the
        caller's credentials with your identity provider or user store, and
        remove any path that sets it without that check. If it already does,
        this is your sign-in: approve it with that reason.
  why   Policy "Every route needs sign-in"

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  medium  ClaimsTable refetches every claim on each keystroke
  apps/web/src/components/ClaimsTable.tsx:61:3

    61 │   useEffect(() => { refetch(); }, [query]);
       │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

  The useEffect depends on query with no debounce, and the endpoint has no
  pagination. Meridian's claims table is 12,400 rows — that's a full scan per
  character typed. It's fine in the demo dataset and will be slow in
  production.

  fix   Debounce to ~250ms, or move the filter server-side. Neither is urgent.
  why   Policy "No unbounded refetch on user input"

  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  1 blocking finding · 3 warnings

  v1.3 went to production on 2 Oct; today's review blocks it. An admin or a security responder who didn't start this review can approve each blocking finding with a reason in Canyon's dashboard; then run this again.
